newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Wegener expects 10 pct EPS growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Wegener expects 10 pct EPS growth in 1997.

text.p: Dutch publisher Wegener NV said on Wednesday it expected to see an increase in 1997 earnings per share of at least 10 percent.

The company earlier posted 1996 net profit of 69.4 million guilders, up from 58.7 million one year earlier. In August it said it expected profit growth in the second half of 1996 to match the 16.1 percent growth of the first half.

"It is expected that revenues will grow both automonously as well as from recent and future acquisitions, and that direct costs might relatively decrease. That constitutes a positive outlook for 1997," Wegener said in a statement.

It added the company did not expect any change in the composition of revenues in 1997 after the "radical change" of last year. It anticipated further growth in advertising revenues from newspaper publishing and acquisitions made late in 1996 would contribute to revenue growth in the music sector.
Wegener said the introduction of new technologoy would result in initial costs during 1997 and that the resultant savings would not be visible until 1998.
"There will be initial costs for implementing new media, including activities on the internet and regional television.
A shut down at a printing plant at Deventer, in the east of the Netherlands would go ahead at the end of 1997 as part of the integration process within the newspaper publishing division.
Further acquisitions are intended, particularly in the direct marketing and music sectors, it added.
